name: Question 6
problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $H(5,7,2)$ and $S(3,4,5).$
worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $H$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=h+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $h$ is the position vector of $H.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $H(5,7,2)$ and $S(3,4,5),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{HS} \\  & =⟨3,4,5⟩-⟨5,7,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,-3,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points H(5,7,2) and S(3,4,5).

a
r=[572]+t[2−32],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[250]+t[−2−33],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[345]+t[−23−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[572]+t[−2−33],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[−2−33]+t[572],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through H and parallel to v is given by r=h+tv, where t∈(−∞,∞) and h is the position vector of H.

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points H(5,7,2) and S(3,4,5), as follows:

v=HS→=⟨3,4,5⟩−⟨5,7,2⟩=⟨−2,−3,3⟩

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

r=[572]+t[−2−33],t∈(−∞,∞).
